children: It's taken Tesla a while, but it finally looks ready to dispense with the steering wheel.

The electric-vehicle maker is set to host a Cybercab event in Austin, Texas, this evening. (Wall Street is still awaiting details for the livestream, which is typically available on X.) It's a significant event for the company. Cybercab, Tesla's purpose-built robo-taxi without pedals or a steering wheel that went into mass production earlier this year, is the culmination of years of work on autonomous driving technology.

The event, which Tesla teased weeks ago, likely signals the introduction of the Cybercab into Tesla's robo-taxi service, which began in Austin in June 2025. Barclays analyst Dan Levy noted in a recent report that Tesla had registered 45 Cybercabs with the Texas Department of Motor Vehicles ahead of the launch.
"We expect event to be lighter on details," added Levy. "Yet growth/scaling targets could be a catalyst, [which] reinforces [the] meme nature of the stock."

Tesla really can't be considered a meme stock given its trillion-dollar valuation, but it often trades more on news and hope than on fundamentals, such as earnings growth. Tesla has grown annual earnings per share since 2022. That could change this year. Analysts expect 2026 earnings per share of $1.69, up three cents from 2025.

The "bull case" for the event is the launch of Cybercabs in Austin, Houston, and Dallas for paid rides, says Morgan Stanley analyst Andrew Percoco. "The market needs to see more than a handful [of] Cybercabs on the road." Fifty-plus is a good number in the days and weeks following the launch. If Tesla does that, Percoco expects a positive stock reaction.

Tesla stock was up 0.8% at $359.86 in premarket trading, while S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average futures were down 0.1% and flat, respectively. Coming into Thursday trading, shares were up only a few dollars from June 2025, shortly after the robo-taxi launch. Investors have been waiting for the business to grow significantly.
The "bear case" for Percoco is that investors are left waiting, with only demonstration rides in Cybercabs and limited fleet deployment in the field.

Whatever happens on Thursday, Cybercab remains important for Tesla stock. It's part of Tesla's strategy to be the low-cost robo-taxi operator, says StoneX analyst Mickey Legg. Lower costs can help Tesla win most of the market share in the nascent self-driving taxi market.

There are still unknowns. Down the road, "the open question is not whether Tesla can build the cheapest robotaxi, but whether a two-seat vehicle priced at a 55% discount to Waymo on the same route can generate the fare per mile required to make the cost advantage translate into contribution margin," added Legg.
Investors will get the answer to some questions on Thursday evening.
